label: input-token detector for o/q/f/0/d/a and <DEL> (context-gated)
explanation: Fires mainly when the current input is one of o, q, f, 0, d, a (in the original phase) or the <DEL> delimiter; these inputs hold ~74% of activation mass. The rate is strongest for o (26%), q (19%), and f (15%), and highest at original positions 2-4 and at <DEL> (11%). Firing is context-gated: precision is only ~0.19, and on the same tokens activation is much more likely and larger when earlier inputs include t (first_tok t has 3.4x lift; the top examples start with t t), and k/y/s/j/2 to a lesser degree. However, a simple seen(...) condition did not capture the gating (F1 <= 0.35). Weaker firing in the copy phase (20% of mass), mostly at recall_idx 0-2 when outputting t/s/j/k. It is rarely active at t=0, late in long sequences, or on other letters like l/c/v/i/1.
